chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
So hasten to good works; wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together

He said: 'Good works' refers to Wilayah (Guardianship), and His Words, the Blessed and Exalted: 'wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together' means the companions of Al-Qaim, three hundred and ten men.
He said: 'And they are, by Allah, a numbered community.'
He said: 'By Allah, they will gather together in a single hour, swiftly like the swift gathering of autumn.'

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The Riser (Al-Qaim, title of the 12th Imam)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together' mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi interprets 'good works' (khayrat) in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:148 specifically as Wilayah, linking the general call to virtue with the specific Shia concept of divine guardianship. It further elucidates the phrase 'wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together' by identifying the 'all' as the 310 companions of Al-Qaim, who will be miraculously gathered in a single hour, likened to the swift gathering of autumn clouds. This interpretation underscores the eschatological significance of the Imam's companions and their instantaneous assembly as a sign of divine power and the culmination of the Mahdi's mission.

en.hubeali: H 14935 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Ismail Bin Jabir, from Abu Khalid, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’farasws
regarding the Statement of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic:
“[2:148] therefore hasten to (do) good works; wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together”.

Heasws said: ‘Good works is a reference to Al-Wilayah, and the Words of the Blessed and the High: “wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together” mean the companions of Al-Qaimasws, three hundred and some ten men’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And they are, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a numbered community’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> they would gather together in a single moment, like clouds in the autumn’.
en.sarwar: 488. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazi’e, from Munzar in Jayfar, from Hisham Bin Saalim who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘Travel when it is cool (time of the day)’. I said, ‘We are afraid of the pests’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘Even if something affects you, it is better for you in view to the fact that you will be safe (from sunstroke), as you are the protected ones (from pets)’.
